author: Benjamin P Taylor

works.title: Peter Block has a deeply irritating habit; he consistently Gives Good Guru and makes you think, damnit.
works.description: Peter Block on relationships, resistance, and what our management and commissioning practices ask of people. What would change if the way we worked embodied the relationships we wanted?
works.author: Benjamin P Taylor

works.title: Where are the systems in ‘systems leadership’?
works.description: Investigating and changing recurring patterns, including our own part in them. A combined essay on leadership development, public health, power, and the conditions that keep problems recurring.
works.author: Benjamin P Taylor

works.title: Is insight easy in #publichealth, but impact hard?
works.description: What turns shared understanding into change in neighbourhoods? Missing authority, resources, and opportunities to learn, with fourteen public-health systems insight briefings.
works.author: Benjamin P Taylor

works.title: Legibility without destruction
works.description: How can government understand what happens in a place without requiring local life to organise itself around a data return? Citizen-held measures, inquiry, assurance, and control.
works.author: Benjamin P Taylor

works.title: Myron’s maxims: participation, power, and the work of change
works.description: An examination of participation, direction, real work, and responsibility. What do useful maxims hide when they are treated as universal truths?
works.author: Benjamin P Taylor

works.title: How will a rewired state resolve disagreements?
works.description: Who decides when neighbourhoods, councils, and regions disagree? Exploring autonomy, a Right to Propose, and whether learning can alter responsibilities and resources.
works.author: Benjamin P Taylor

works.title: My pessimistic prediction for English local government: abolish two tiers, then recreate them at a larger scale, with less local autonomy. Tell me I’m wrong?
works.description: A forecast that devolution could rebuild hierarchy at a larger scale, and an argument for protected local powers and continuing negotiation. A prediction, rather than an announced settlement.
works.author: Benjamin P Taylor

works.title: No escape, no prison – on other perspectives on systems | cybernetics | complexity
works.description: Stability, change, and the limits of our ways of seeing. A response to criticism of the six-diagram account, with the longer original essay, diagrams, and self-critique.
works.author: Benjamin P Taylor

relatedLinks.title: The fly-bottle is where the work happens: full essay and diagrams
